extracted.intended_audience: SEC registrants, securities lawyers, corporate compliance officers, and investors interested in SEC climate-related disclosure rules
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and accommodations in the SEC's final rules for climate-related disclosures, including which filings and registrants are covered, structured data tagging (Inline XBRL) requirements, liability treatment, exemptions, and phased compliance dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of covered filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules require registrants that file Exchange Act annual reports on Forms 10-K, and Securities Act and Exchange Act registration statements on Form 10 and Forms S-1, S-4 (except as provided), or S-11, as applicable, to include the climate-related disclosures required by the final rules. Foreign private issuers filing on Form 20-F and Securities Act registration statements on Form F-1 or Form F-4 (except as provided) must provide the same climate-related disclosures as domestic registrants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: climate-related risks are financial risks and should be treated like other business and financial information; including disclosures in familiar forms promotes transparency and comparability. The Commission declined to adopt a new, separate form for climate disclosures and may consider substituted compliance with other jurisdictions in the future depending on developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption for private target companies in business combinations (Forms S-4/F-4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rules will not apply to private companies that are parties to business combination transactions, as defined by Securities Act Rule 165(f), involving a securities offering registered on Forms S-4 and F-4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: acknowledging burdens and timing impacts of requiring private targets to prepare climate disclosure in addition to other Regulation S-K/S-X requirements; avoids discouraging business combination activity and delays in transaction timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: No interim updating requirement in Form 10-Q (and limited Form 6-K updates)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules will not require registrants to disclose any material change to the climate-related disclosures provided in a registration statement or annual report in its Form 10-Q or, in certain circumstances, Form 6-K for a foreign private issuer that does not report on domestic forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change from the proposal responds to commenters concerned about compliance costs and limited investor value from intra-year updates; mitigates compliance burden by aligning with annual reporting practice in other contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of MJDS filers (Canadian Form 40-F filers)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules will not apply to Canadian registrants that use the Multi-Jurisdictional Disclosure System (MJDS) and file Exchange Act registration statements and annual reports on Form 40-F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: consistent with MJDS purpose to allow Canadian registrants to follow home-jurisdiction rules; commenters note CSA Proposed Instrument modeled on TCFD would provide similar disclosure once finalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asset-backed securities issuer exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules will not apply to asset-backed securities issuers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: unique market structure of ABS where investor disclosures focus on pool credit quality and payment performance rather than sponsor commitments; the Commission may consider tailored ABS climate disclosure rules in a future rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of SRCs and EGCs as to GHG Scopes 1 and 2
rubrics_metrics.description: Most of the final rules apply to Smaller Reporting Companies (SRCs) and Emerging Growth Companies (EGCs), except SRCs and EGCs are exempted from the disclosure requirements requiring Scopes 1 and 2 emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: to reduce proportionally greater compliance burden on smaller and early-stage registrants; SRCs and EGCs remain subject to other aspects of the final rules. Additional accommodations include materiality qualifiers, less prescriptive provisions, and extended phase-ins based on filer status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of BDCs, REITs, and certain insurance issuers (no blanket exemptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules do not exempt BDCs, REITs, or issuers of registered non-variable insurance contracts from the requirements; these entities may have limited disclosure obligations to the extent climate-related risks are not material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission view: differences from operating companies are not significant enough to warrant exclusion; streamlined/modified rules and materiality limitation should limit burden when climate risk is immaterial. Some timing accommodations may apply where applicability arises solely from certain offerings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of Forms S-8 and 11-K
rubrics_metrics.description: As proposed and finalized, the final rules will not apply to disclosures in Forms S-8 and 11-K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No commenters addressed Form 11-K applicability in detail; the Commission keeps these forms outside the scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured data requirement: Inline XBRL tagging for climate disclosures (Item 1508)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules require registrants to tag climate-related disclosures in Inline XBRL in accordance with Rule 405 of Regulation S-T and the EDGAR Filer Manual, including both block text tagging and detail tagging of narrative and quantitative disclosures provided pursuant to subpart 1500 of Regulation S-K and Article 14 of Regulation S-X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: machine-readable tagging enables automated extraction, comparison across periods and registrants, aggregation, filtering, and analysis, improving usefulness and comparability. Commission concluded the existing Inline XBRL language is familiar and should be required rather than permitting registrant choice or voluntary tagging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tag both narrative and quantitative disclosures (detail and block text tagging)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters and the Commission supported tagging of both quantitative climate-related metrics and qualitative climate-related disclosures (narrative), including block text and detail tagging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tagging narrative and quantitative information expedites aggregation and synthesis, increases accessibility, and is necessary to achieve efficiencies in capital markets as climate-related disclosures grow in volume. Some commenters warned against custom tags to preserve comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxonomy development, avoiding custom tags, and interoperability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will develop a draft taxonomy for the final rules, make it available for public comment, and incorporate a final taxonomy into EDGAR; it will seek to incorporate elements from third-party taxonomies (e.g., ISSB) to promote interoperability and avoid excessive custom tagging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concern: registrants creating custom tags could erode comparability and data quality. Commission will delay LAF tagging compliance one year after initial compliance to allow taxonomy finalization and reduce custom tagging. Interoperability with international standards is emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: No voluntary tagging; single structured data language required
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will not permit voluntary tagging or registrant selection of a structured data language; Inline XBRL tagging is mandatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: voluntary tagging or permitting multiple languages would likely reduce data completeness and interoperability, hindering usability and comparability for investors and stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured data compliance timing and phased tagging deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: For LAFs (Large Accelerated Filers), compliance with the structured data requirements for subpart 1500 disclosures is required one year after initial compliance with the disclosure requirements; other categories of filers must comply with tagging upon their initial compliance with subpart 1500. No separate later compliance date for non-LAF registrants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: LAFs have the earliest compliance date and delaying tagging by one year helps reduce need for custom tags and eases adoption; other filers have later overall compliance dates. Tagging deadlines align with the registrant-specific initial compliance dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of climate-related disclosures as 'filed' (liability exposure)
rubrics_metrics.description: The climate-related disclosures provided pursuant to the final rules will be treated as 'filed' and therefore subject to potential liability under Exchange Act section 18 and, if included or incorporated by reference into a Securities Act registration statement, Securities Act section 11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: treating disclosures as filed promotes accuracy and consistency and deters greenwashing. The Commission considered commenters' concerns about complexities and evolving methodologies (especially Scope 3) and adopted modifications (limiting GHG scope, materiality qualifiers, PSLRA safe harbor, transition periods) to mitigate liability concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications to mitigate burden and liability (scope limits, materiality qualifiers, PSLRA safe harbor, transition periods)
rubrics_metrics.description: To address concerns about methodology uncertainty and compliance burden, the final rules include modifications: limiting the scope of the GHG emissions disclosure requirement; revising provisions so certain disclosures (strategy, targets and goals, metrics) are required only when material; adding a PSLRA safe harbor for several types of climate-related disclosures; and providing transition periods based on filer status and content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These changes were intended to reduce burdens and liability exposure while preserving investor access to material climate information. They support the decision to treat disclosures as filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance phase-in schedule based on filer status (LAFs, AFs, NAFs, SRCs, EGCs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission proposed and adopted phase-in dates that differ based on a registrant's filing status or status as an SRC, recognizing many registrants will need time to build systems, controls, and procedures; LAFs are first, AFs/NAFs have additional time, and SRCs have the greatest amount of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: allow time to prepare, especially for smaller registrants; EGCs and SRCs receive particular accommodations (e.g., exemption from Scopes 1/2 and extended phase-ins). The proposing release included an illustrative table of phase-ins assuming a December 2022 effective date and December 31 fiscal year-end.

rubrics_metrics.name: No blanket exemption for IPO registrants; accommodations instead
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission is not providing an exemption or transitional relief for registrants engaged in an IPO; instead, streamlined requirements, accommodations, exemption of EGCs from Scopes 1/2, and longer transition periods for SRCs/EGCs are intended to address concerns about chilling capital formation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: preserve investor protections and ensure information availability at all stages of capital formation while seeking to limit burdens on new registrants through scaled accommodations and longer transition periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial emissions disclosure limited to one year for first-time reporters
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial filings from registrants that are not SRCs or EGCs and that determine they have material Scope 1 and/or Scope 2 emissions will only be required to provide emissions data for one year because they will not have previously provided such disclosure in a Commission filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduces burden on initial reporters who lack prior Commission-filed emissions history; subsequent reporting obligations will follow applicable phase-in and content rules.
